pr_title: Fix #453: Setting historySize=32767 causes WindowsTerminal to hang
pr_body:
With this change, setting the scrollback history size (number of scrollback rows) to more than about 32,000 will no longer cause Windows Terminal to hang forever.

The problem was indeed what @zadjii-msft said it might be in the bug - the history size is persisted into profiles.json as a 32-bit signed integer (well, really a JSON/JS number, but the internal data models use 32-bit ints), but was being coerced without overflow checks into 16 bits, and the bug was the overflow in question. The fix was to clamp the history size read in to a non-negative 16-bit signed integer.

I also took the liberty of adding similar overflow/underflow clamping for the initial number of rows and columns in the window.

Testing:
- manual
- CI build and test passes, including new unit tests I added:
  https://dev.azure.com/ms/Terminal/_build/results?buildId=15717
   (note: the TerminalControl changes aren't currently tested as I couldn't find any existing test scaffolding)

No doc changes made or required
Fixes #453

* What you're doing and what's happening: Setting historySize to 32767 (0x7FFF) via profile.json settings. I tried 32766 and that also failed, but 32000 was fine. So something on the fringes there is busted.

comments:
That makes sense. 

Currently I think we're using a `short` for the history size, and this is a carry-over from the conhost code. 

We should probably sanitize that input - if someone uses a value larger than `SHORT_MAX`, we should just clamp it when we create the buffer.

review_comments: Any reason that this firs macro just expands into the second? Couldn't it just be `#define WCS(x) L#x`?

Unfortunately not, because then `WCS(SHRT_MAX)` would expand to `LSHRT_MAX` because `SHRT_MAX` is itself a macro.

I got this "trick" (although I hesitate to use that word with any kind of C preprocessor magic) from here: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/Stringizing.html
woah well that's... insane, but I get it. Such is life using C macros :P

Note that regardless of this change, Terminal still crashes on startup if you have more than a few thousand rows in the `initialRows` setting, for reasons unrelated to this bug fix (since technically the GitHub issue is only about the `historySize` setting). I'll open a separate GitHub issue for that bug.
Per the other comment, I think `std::clamp` would really get the job done here.
